summary: ECHOES OF SPACE is an interactive storytelling and simulation project that brings forgotten NASA spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment back to life through their voices, mission histories, and imagined final messages inspired by documented events. Our project explores their journeys, scientific discoveries, challenges, and lasting contributions to space exploration. Through an educational presentation and simulation, we aim to help students understand the importance of these forgotten explorers and connect emotionally with their stories. We used digital presentation and development tools to create our project, with Gemini providing limited assistance in refining content, improving presentation quality, and adding finishing touches.
details:
Project Title: Ghost Signals: Space Graveyard Explorer

High-Level Summary: An interactive "space archaeology" web experience that lets school-age explorers tune into faint radio echoes from NASA’s retired spacecraft on the Moon, Mars, and deep space—bringing each machine’s first-person story and scientific legacy back to life.

Detailed Project Description: Since the 1960s, NASA has left dozens of pioneering rovers, landers, and probes across the solar system after their primary missions ended. For young learners, museum lists and mission logs can feel distant and technical. Ghost Signals: Space Graveyard Explorer reframes space history as an interactive detective mission.

Players filter across three zones—The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space—and click on eight real NASA artifacts (including the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10, and Dawn) to decode their residual telemetry. Each artifact features real coordinates, mission lifespans, a synthesized first-person audio transmission, and a breakdown of the breakthrough science it made possible, culminating in a Space Archaeologist certification quiz.

NASA Data & Resources Referenced:

  • NASA Science: Solar System Exploration & Mission Archives (Apollo, Surveyor, Mars Exploration Rovers, InSight, Mars 2020/Ingenuity, Pioneer 10, Dawn)
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS): Mission telemetry and coordinates
  • NASA Image and Video Library (images.nasa.gov): Official public-domain images used for the artifact cards and modal backgrounds
